resources.string: Elamon shows a computer\'s load, temperatures, memory, processes and monitors live, and controls its links, media and power. The computer runs a small service, elamond, that only paired phones can reach.
Install the Elamon service, elamond, on the computer (Linux). In a terminal there, as yourself, not root:
It installs elamond and starts it. Then run as root the commands it prints. On NixOS, use the module instead: Step-by-step guide below.
Run this on the computer. It shows a QR code and a six-digit code:
Point this phone\'s camera at the QR code, or tap Add computer and enter the code.
The easiest way: run elamond pair on the computer and point the phone\'s camera at the QR code it shows.
Or enter the computer\'s address, then the six-digit code.
Check that these digits match the certificate line elamond pair shows on the computer:

The computer couldn\'t be told. To remove this phone there, run elamond revoke on it (elamond clients lists the phones).
The computer no longer accepts it, maybe after elamond revoke. Run elamond pair on the computer and pair again.

This phone can no longer read its key for the computer, as happens when the phone\'s key store was reset. Run elamond pair on the computer and pair again; elamond revoke there removes the old pairing.
This happens when the Elamon service\'s data was reset or reinstalled, but also when something else pretends to be the computer. If you didn\'t reset it, check your network before pairing again.
The computer may be off or asleep, the Elamon service not running, or the phone on another network. Elamon keeps trying.

Elamon has two parts: this app, and elamond, a small service on the computer you want to watch. It needs no root and runs as your user. Almost everything is set on the computer; the app draws what the service describes.
On NixOS, use the module instead. Add the project to your flake\'s inputs:
Import its module and turn the service on. openFirewall opens the ports; linger keeps the service running while you\'re logged out. For Home Manager, see the full guide.
One command installs the service for your user (run it as yourself, not root) and runs elamond setup, which prints the few commands that need root:
On NixOS, the openFirewall option above does it. Without it:
Without a firewall nothing needs opening. Otherwise open TCP %1$s (the service) and UDP %2$s (mDNS, so the app can find the computer on the local network) in the one you use.
It shows a QR code and a six-digit code, good for five minutes. Scan the QR code with the phone\'s camera and open the link: that pairs in one tap.

Or in this app tap the computer under Found on this network, or Add computer and its address, and enter the code. Check that the certificate digits the app shows match the Certificate line on the computer.
Then elamond pair asks on the computer: Allow? [y/N]. Answer y if the phone is yours, and keep elamond pair running until the phone is paired.
Tabs, widgets, the theme, animations (all of them or none), confirmations and how often readings come are the computer\'s: the profile it gives this phone. Settings names it and where it is changed.
This phone\'s own, under Settings → Display: the app\'s scale, and a theme that stays whatever the computers say. The app opens on the computer you opened last; Back goes to the list.

Under Hyprland, Control\'s Monitors group turns each monitor and its picture on and off and sets its brightness. Turning off the last screen that still shows a picture asks for its name to be typed first, so the computer isn\'t left dark by a slip.
5. Widget, tiles and the computer\'s card

The home-screen widget shows a computer\'s readings: the values, gauges, statuses, lists and texts of a dashboard, its gauges as small rings. It reads them in the background every so often (15 minutes at the least) and at once when tapped; the computer\'s name on it opens the computer here. Out of reach, it keeps the last readings, faded, with their time. With several computers paired, adding it asks which one it shows.

Four Quick Settings tiles, Elamon tile 1 to 4, run the first four buttons and toggles of a dashboard, a switch showing whether it is on. A locked phone is unlocked first, and what an action asks in the app (a confirmation, unlocking, a name to type) it asks over the panel too. With several computers, Settings says which one the tiles act on.
The computer\'s card on the home screen can show a dashboard of its own, its buttons and toggles as quick actions; without one, the first figures of the first tab.
Which dashboards they show is the computer\'s to say, in the android table of the profile it gives this phone (Settings names it). Nothing set, the widget says so and the tiles have no action:

The computer can tell what happens to it: a disk nearly full, a unit that failed, a laptop\'s battery low, a UPS on battery. Rules in its settings make these events. The Events page, behind Control\'s Events button, lists them with a level to filter by and a search, as does any page the computer\'s settings give a log of events.

Notifications don\'t come from this app, which asks for no permission to show any. The service sends events to an ntfy topic set up in the computer\'s settings, and the ntfy app on this phone shows them, whether Elamon is open or not.

Which rules there are, their limits and texts, and what is sent are all the computer\'s settings: by default, events from level warning up, without the names of units, disks or the computer. A script makes an event of its own words:

A phone the computer gives the role owner edits its dashboards and the tabs of its profiles here, in forms, with no settings file to write: in a computer\'s menu, Edit dashboard, New dashboard and Edit tabs. The computer gives the role (elamond clients role ID owner), and its Elamon service has to be 0.11 or newer, with the editor on in its settings.

Edit shows the dashboard as it looks. Touch and hold a widget\'s handle, then drag it to another\'s place; tap a widget for its settings and its width; Add widget offers what the computer can show, each with an example. What the forms offer, the computer describes. Buttons, switches and a table\'s rows only pick an action the computer\'s settings already have: the editor writes no commands.

Saving unlocks the phone first, whatever the profile asks before actions: it changes the computer\'s settings. The computer checks them, then writes what you saved to a settings file of its own, over the others:

Back to the files takes a dashboard or a profile\'s tabs out of that file again, as the other files have them; a dashboard only that file has is deleted instead. If it was changed elsewhere meanwhile (the computer\'s web page, another phone), the editor says so and keeps your changes until you choose.
The rest of the admin panel (the settings files, the paired phones, pairing, holding control off) is the computer\'s web page, in a browser on its address:
Settings, dashboards, the control panel, roles, backups and troubleshooting are in the full guide, online.
